rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken Cantonese word for a large handled drinking cup.

example.english: I drink coffee from a mug.
example.jyutping: ngo5 jung6 go3 mak1 jam2 gaa3 fe1

rows.note: Use this for a person who is easily cheated or taken advantage of, rather than merely unintelligent.

example.english: They’re such a mug; people cheat them all the time.
example.traditional: 佢真係水魚，成日畀人呃。
example.jyutping: keoi5 zan1 hai6 seoi2 jyu4 seng4 jat6 bei2 jan4 aak1

rows.note: Use this as a colloquial insult for a stupid or contemptible person.

example.jyutping: nei5 m4 hou2 gam3 ngong6 gau1 laa1

rows.note: 打劫 is what people say in daily speech for robbing someone, including a street mugging.

example.english: Someone tried to mug him last night.
example.jyutping: kam4 maan5 jau5 jan4 soeng2 daa2 gip3 keoi5

rows.note: 搶劫 is the more formal word, used in police reports and news; in casual talk people prefer 打劫.

example.english: The police caught the man who tried to mug her.
example.traditional: 警察捉到想搶劫佢嗰個男人。
example.jyutping: ging2 caat3 zuk1 dou3 soeng2 coeng2 gip3 keoi5 go2 go3 naam4 jan2
